summary:
For our project, we developed an interactive website called "Some Explorers Never Came Home" featuring 20 stories of NASA’s and space agencies' discarded equipment and spacecraft that remained on the Moon, Mars, and deep space after completing their missions.
Guided by a virtual "NASA Agent," users can browse an interactive visual gallery where clicking on any spacecraft opens a dedicated story page detailing its launch, mission goals, and current status. This directly addresses the "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge by turning space history into an engaging UI/UX storytelling experience that honors pioneering machines and makes space exploration accessible to everyone
details:
Project Description: "Some Explorers Never Came Home" is an interactive web archive designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, highlighting 20 historic spacecraft that remained in space after completing their missions.

How it Works & Impact: Guided by a virtual NASA Agent, users can explore detailed profiles of these iconic missions, discovering their full stories, launch histories, and scientific legacies. The project bridges space history and public education, turning historical exploration data into an immersive, inspiring digital experience .

Tools & Technologies: Developed using clean web design principles, HTML/CSS/JavaScript frameworks, and UI/UX design workflows to ensure an intuitive and engaging user interface

Creativity: By giving "abandoned" or permanent space explorers a dedicated digital voice and narrative archive, we offer a unique emotional and educational perspective on humanity's footprint in space.
